thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty fired: P0 - inference-queue backlog rising (us-east1). Alert: queue_depth > 80% for 6m, avg latency spikes, autoscaler not increasing fast enough. PD INC12345 - https://pagerduty.example/INC12345

jess-h: acked. I'm oncall. tagging @akash and @maya-infra. any quick wins to stop customer impact? :eyes:

akash: seeing controller logs show scale decisions saturated. controller is logging 'scale throttled by provisioner' and several `FailedCreate` from nodes. sharing snippets:
```
E0323 12:34:21 scale_controller.go:245] desired=120 observed=45 reason="insufficient nodes: 15 PendingCreation, 10 InsufficientQuota"
W0323 12:34:35 provisioner.go:98] provision request throttled by cloudprovider (rate limit)
```

maya-infra: confirmed - nodepool us-east1-workers is hitting cloud API rate limits. Cloud provider slow to return new instances; spot interruptions + quota bump in progress but not applied yet. I've opened support ticket and requested expedited quota.

tom-runtime: kv cache cold is amplifying load — many requests missing prefix cache, so effective token work per request is high. two immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily increase replicas/HPAs, 2) route low-priority traffic to smaller model variant.

jess-h: let's do both. akash, can you manual-scale HPA and replicas? maya, can you bump node pool min and enable faster provisioning? tom, prepare route override payload. we'll keep PD on.

akash: doing manual scale now. running:
```
kubectl -n inference scale deploy inference-worker --replicas=80
kubectl -n inference patch hpa inference-worker-hpa -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":140}}'
kubectl -n inference rollout status deploy/inference-worker
```

akash: scale command returned 'ScalingReplicaSet... - scaled'. seeing new pods PendingImagePull -> ContainerCreating. still waiting on nodes. :frowning:

maya-infra: issuing nodepool resize via cloud API (requested emergency increase). running:
```
gcloud container clusters update redwood-us-east1 --region us-east1 --update-addons=HorizontalPodAutoscaling
gcloud container node-pools resize redwood-us-east1-workers --region us-east1 --num-nodes=90
```
support ticket 987654 opened with cloud provider. ETA unknown but requested high priority.

pd-bot: PagerDuty: INC12345 acknowledged by jess-h. Escalation timer paused.

tom-runtime: preparing route override. sample POST to control plane:
```
POST https://console.redwood/api/v1/route/overrides
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "route": "inference:predict",
  "policy": "temporary_fallback",
  "fallback_model": "redwood-small-quantized-v2",
  "weight": 0.5
}
```
This will shift 50% of traffic to smaller model to reduce per-request GPU time. I'll hold on apply until akash confirms pods a bit healthier.

akash: pods are coming up - 45/80 running. CPU per-pod still high (~85%) due to kv cache cold misses. manual scale helped a bit: queue depth dropping from 88% -> 65% over last 4m.

jess-h: @tom-runtime go ahead with a 30% shift now. monitor latency and error rate closely.

tom-runtime: applied 30% route shift. response: 
- 1m after: tail latency median down ~12%
- errors stable 

maya-infra: cloud provider replied: provisioning rate-limit lifted for short window. additional nodes incoming. increasing nodepool to 120 temporarily.

akash: nodes registering. new pods scheduled. `kubectl get nodes` shows +35 nodes in the last 6m. queue depth now 32%.

jess-h: great. continue to observe. I want an ETA to full recovery and plan to update PD status.

pd-bot: PagerDuty: INC12345 status updated: Acknowledged -> Investigating. Next escalation in 40m if not resolved.

akash: detailed check: controller still logging a few throttles but not blocking. memory pressure on a subset of pods, restarted one. sample recent logs:
```
I0323 12:45:02 dispatcher.go:101] processed 120 req/s
E0323 12:45:18 allocator.go:77] eviction predicted for pod/inference-worker-xyz, memory=85%
```
Mitigations done: manual scale, hpa max raised, route override, nodepool resized, spot fallback disabled for critical pool.

tom-runtime: recommendation: post-incident followup to tune autoscaler rate limits, increase HPA stabilization windows, and pre-warm kv cache during release windows. I'll add to incident doc.

jess-h: customer impact: partial degradation for 12 minutes at peak; some requests experienced 2-3x latency; no large-scale errors or data loss. We'll update status page with brief note.

maya-infra: cloud provider confirmed nodes are stable. I'll keep resize for another 30m then scaleback.

akash: monitoring shows sustained queue depth < 35% and p99 latency returning to baseline. closing the PD escalation for now.

pd-bot: PagerDuty: INC12345 - status set to Resolved by jess-h.

jess-h: thanks team. quick action worked. follow-ups: (1) autoscaler tuning (akash + maya), (2) route fallback runbook additions (tom), (3) postmortem doc and customer comms (I'll own). tagging for follow-up. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident log appended: INC12345 — capacity exhaustion due to cloud provisioner throttle. Actions: manual scale, route fallback, nodepool emergency resize, provider support ticket.

akash: copying logs and metrics to incident doc now.

maya-infra: I'll schedule a capacity rehearsal next week to test provisioning under load.

tom-runtime: will add automated small-model fallback in the router as a circuit-breaker to trigger when queue_depth > 70% for >5m.

jess-h: closing thread. if regressions, re-open PD. thanks all :raised_hands:
